temporal_modules_reason: There is no dataset to split; the Python code only orchestrates tests and benchmarks of the TypeScript engine.
non_goals: A distributed scheduler. Work is simulated in one process with virtual time; there are no workers, queues or persistence.
Fastest possible ordering. The benchmarks establish growth rates and relative cost, not records.
risks: Timings depend on the machine and on what else was running; the scaling exponents are more stable than the milliseconds.
Random graphs have uniform structure, while real pipelines are shallower and more branched.
Mutation testing only shows that the planted bugs are caught, not that no other bug exists.
The executor's failure model is independent per attempt; correlated failures are not simulated.
lessons: Keeping the slow, obviously correct implementation as an oracle found a real bug in the fast rewrite.
Tests that pass on correct code are only evidence once they have been shown to fail on broken code.
A benchmark can expose a scaling problem that no correctness test will: the first executor was correct and quadratic.
Types can be tested too: an @ts-expect-error that stops failing is a regression the compiler reports.
